name: Familial Atrial Standstill

criteria.description: Electrocardiographic evidence of absence of atrial electrical activity (no P waves)
Persistent bradycardia with junctional or ventricular escape rhythm
Positive family history of atrial standstill or sudden cardiac death
Failure to capture atrial myocardium on pacing attempts
Echocardiographic evidence of absent atrial contraction

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria: absence of atrial electrical activity on ECG, persistent bradycardia with escape rhythm, and positive family history
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may support diagnosis but is not mandatory

pathognomonic.notes: Identified on ECG as absent P waves

pathognomonic.symptomName: Severe bradycardia due to atrial standstill
searchTerms: very slow heartbeat from atrial pause
extremely slow heart rate due to atrial inactivity
severe slow pulse from atrial standstill

pathognomonic.notes: Transient loss of consciousness due to cerebral hypoperfusion
searchTerms: passing out due to slow heartbeat

occasional.notes: Due to atrial mechanical failure and ventricular dysfunction

occasional.symptomName: Palpitations due to junctional escape rhythm
searchTerms: feeling heart racing from junctional beats

rare.notes: Due to atrial standstill-related thrombus formation
searchTerms: brain stroke or blood clot traveling in body
stroke or systemic blood clot event

laboratory: Possible elevated brain natriuretic peptide (BNP) in heart failure
imaging: Echocardiography showing absence of atrial contraction
ECG demonstrating absence of P waves and junctional or ventricular escape rhythm
genetic: Mutations in SCN5A gene associated with familial atrial standstill
other: Electrophysiological studies confirming atrial electrical inactivity
Failure of atrial capture on pacing

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of sinus node dysfunction with preserved atrial activity
P waves present but abnormal sinus rhythm
Presence of P waves with AV conduction delay or block
Bradycardia due to AV node dysfunction rather than atrial standstill
Irregularly irregular rhythm with fibrillatory waves instead of absent atrial activity
Presence of chaotic atrial electrical activity

redFlags: Family history of sudden cardiac death
references: Watanabe H, et al. Familial atrial standstill associated with SCN5A mutation. Circulation. 2008;117(3): 340-346.
Miyamoto K, et al. Clinical features and management of atrial standstill. J Cardiol. 2019;73(1): 1-7.
